extracted.intended_audience: Applicants and grantees seeking NIMH/NIH research grant funding (including new investigators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, submitting, and managing research grant applications to NIMH/NIH, including eligibility, FOA types, review and funding decisions, administrative systems, and resubmission rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: New investigator key elements
rubrics_metrics.description: New investigators need information on Research Topics (NIMH research areas; types of grant mechanisms; recent funding opportunity announcements) and the Research Process for Submission (how to contact a program officer; which forms and applications to use; what the deadlines for submission are; how the review process works).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is strongly recommended you contact a program officer before beginning an application. Be sure to allow plenty of time to complete an application. Familiarize yourself with NIMH research areas, applicable grant mechanisms, and current FOAs before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of Funding Opportunity Announcements (FOAs)
rubrics_metrics.description: FOAs include Program Announcements (PAs) and Requests for Applications (RFAs); there are also special PA types known as PARs and PASs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the Research Funding Opportunities page for further details and to find current FOAs relevant to your work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal investigator (PI) eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Any individual with the skills, knowledge, and resources necessary to carry out NIMH-relevant research may work with his or her institution to develop a grant application. Individuals from underrepresented racial and ethnic groups and individuals with disabilities are encouraged to apply. Applications from investigators at foreign institutions are accepted, but some programs have citizenship/residency requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates for diversity supplements, NRSA trainees at any level, and candidates for career awards must be citizens or permanent residents. Any special eligibility criteria for PIs, staff, or participants will be specified in the FOA under Eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individuals not eligible to be PIs (common exclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons pursuing training solely to provide mental health services; persons at the high school level; undergraduates; persons pursuing master's level degrees only; persons who lack an institutional affiliation are not eligible to be PIs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High school students and undergraduates may be supported through Diversity Supplements submitted by PIs of grants. An eligible institution is necessary to administer any grant; see specific FOAs for institutional eligibility details. Those interested in clinical training should contact the Center for Mental Health Services (SAMHSA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional eligibility requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An eligible institution is necessary to administer any grant; eligible institutions may be domestic or foreign, public or private, non-profit or for-profit, and may include government agencies, institutions of higher education, and hospitals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific FOAs will list institutional eligibility; if you lack an institutional affiliation you generally cannot be awarded a grant directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Components of a complete NIH grant number
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete NIH grant number indicates the Type Code, Activity Code, Institute Code, Serial Number, Grant Year, and possibly a Suffix. Example: 1-R01-MH99999-01A1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type codes: 1 = new/first time; 2 = competing continuation (requires peer review); 5 = non-competing continuation (administrative review/progress report). Activity codes indicate mechanism (e.g., R01, R03, R13, K, T). Institute codes are two-letter identifiers (e.g., MH = NIMH). Serial number uniquely identifies the project and remains the same while active. Grant year '01' indicates first year. Suffix 'A1' indicates an amended/resubmission application; R01 may be submitted up to three times (A2 is the last amended version permitted). Other suffixes (e.g., S1) refer to competing supplement requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH eRA Commons usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The eRA Commons is a web interface where NIH and the grantee community conduct extramural research administration business electronically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registering and using eRA Commons is part of NIH/NIH grant administration workflows (applications, status, progress reports).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review assignment and committees
rubrics_metrics.description: There are many different review committees. Assignment to a review committee may be suggested by the applicant, but the final decision is made by the NIH Center for Scientific Review (CSR), often in consultation with the NIMH referral office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the referral office (nimhreferral@mail.nih.gov) for questions about assignment. Understand that CSR has final say on study section/referral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding decisions are not guaranteed by score or percentile
rubrics_metrics.description: A particular score or percentile ranking does not guarantee funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other considerations besides score/percentile include institute and division priorities, balance in the existing research portfolio, and availability of funds. Refer to the Funding Strategy for Research Grants for current fiscal-year decision factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progress report due dates and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Due dates for progress reports are dictated by the individual grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay attention to due dates; a late progress report can delay and possibly reduce your award.

rubrics_metrics.name: If not funded — resubmission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally an application can be submitted up to a total of three times (varies by situation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the Program Officer about the resubmission process. Suffixes such as A1 indicate amended/resubmitted applications; review the specific FOA and NIH rules for allowable resubmissions for your mechanism (e.g., R01 limits).
